chapter: California, Art Tatum and Lionel Hampton
title: Art Tatum shows him the changes to Sweet Lorraine
summary: At a jam session, Thompson struggled with Sweet Lorraine until Art Tatum gently showed him the chord progressions.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: I played occasionally although I was a little bit ashamed to follow these men. Occasionally before they came I would have enough nerve to sit down and play, because my friend encouraged me, and they all were very encouraging. But I got to know Art Tatum there briefly at the house, and then I remember one time I was playing in a club where they had these jam sessions and I didn't know the chord changes to the "Sweet Lorraine". As I said at this time I was still studying and really learning, you know, these chord progressions and changes, which is the basics of playing jazz music or any ad lib music. You must know the chord progressions, and I didn't know this at that time.
I was very, very studiously learning these songs, and learning progressions and I was sitting there playing one

night, alone, or with a drummer, or some one or two musicians, at this jam session, and I was trying to play 'Sweet Lorraine,' and I was playing it to the best of my ability, which wasn't correct, very evidently. And I got this voice behind me which I recognized to be Art Tatum. It was the most frightening thing I'd ever heard in my life, when it first happened. He said, oh, Charlie, that's not the way it goes, (let me show you.) He sort of suggested that I slide over and he sat down and he showed me how to play 'Sweet Lorraine' in the chord progressions, and showed me how to learn to play progressions on the piano.

Now, this is something that -- a rare occasion that a man so great and so wonderful would take the time. You know, like a lot of guys would either make gesture of it or try to make a fool or something like that, or embarrass you by it. You know, but the man was just so gentle and kind, and he showed me why I was wrong and showed me how to play it right. And from then on I learned many things from Art Tatum. Unfortunately I didn't ever get to be as closest friends [at home,] although just before he died, in the act of actually becoming close to Art Tatum --
